historical_reviews.deepseek: Generic logs cannot prove persistence, bounded event generation or cleanup.

historical_reviews.related_cases: Row 49 one-shot must disarm after one event; this row intentionally remains armed, so it needs a bounded trigger count and explicit clear proof. Row 51 changes severity to UCE.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Persistent fault state requires an approved activation window, stop command, maximum events and independent residual-state verification.

original_test_intent: Verify bounded persistent correctable DRAM injection on each required slot, showing repeated attributable CE generation only during the approved window and complete cessation after an explicit clear operation.
original_method: Map each physical slot to a documented target tuple; select one RAS profile; capture counters and injector status; arm persistent mode for one tuple; run an approved synthetic access sequence with maximum count/time; prove repeated corrected events at the mapped target; issue the vendor-defined clear/disable command; repeat a verification access proving counters no longer advance; restore BIOS/HDT state and inspect memory health before any next slot.
manual_activity: The FAE maps the target, defines activation bounds and trigger, arms persistent CE, monitors event count, executes the authoritative clear and proves no residual injection before restoration.
required_inputs: Slot-to-socket/die/UMC/channel/rank map and approved replacement/meaning for 0:0:3
Tool/spec version/hash/license and persistent mode activation/status/clear syntax
Synthetic trigger workload, maximum events, duration/rate and threshold margin
Exact corrected-event counters/location plus expected repeated pattern
DRAM-versus-MCA profile choice and FFFE/FFE threshold interaction
Abort limits, emergency clear, timeout, recovery and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated ECC SUT with OOB console and prevalidated emergency clear/recovery
Never arm persistent mode without a verified stop command and independent status/counter observation
Bound event count/time below escalation thresholds; stop on storm, wrong slot, UCE, reset, poison or health loss
Prove a post-clear trigger produces no new event before leaving the test
No automatic retry; clear injector first, then restore/diff BIOS/HDT state
agent_execution_scope: Validate topology, package clear path, thresholds, trigger bounds, profile and evidence oracle
Collect read-only injector status, counters, transcript, OS/BMC events and post-clear health
Do not select tuple/profile, arm persistent mode, trigger faults, clear/recover automatically, repeat or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target and bounded persistent exposure
Provide activation/status/clear commands and emergency stop
Approve profile/threshold/event oracle and supervise run
Verify residual state, restore and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A log tail may show corrected events but cannot prove their count/rate, persistent activation or successful clear.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Arm persistent CE only on one mapped tuple with maximum count/time monitoring, run the approved trigger, then issue the documented clear and prove a subsequent trigger yields no new event.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: errormode 0, tuple 0:0:3, setinjectionmode 1, mcapolling 0, errortype 0, two profiles, slots 1~N and 60/60 minutes remain preserved; missing bounds and clear syntax are explicit gaps.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat persistent CE as a time/count-bounded state machine: baseline, arm, controlled repeated triggers, stop, clear and negative residual test.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds activation status, rate/count limits, threshold margin, authoritative clear, emergency stop and post-clear negative evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Tool PASS and repeated logs cannot prove safe persistence or that the injector was actually cleared.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unbounded persistent CE may cross thresholds, flood logs, escalate severity, reset the host or contaminate later tests.

project_override_considerations: If closing the tool automatically clears mode 1, provide vendor proof and verify status/counters independently. Otherwise the explicit clear command is mandatory before the case can execute.
expected_evidence: Exact identity, topology and approved tuple
Profile/tool/spec plus threshold and exposure limits
Pre-arm status/counters and full arm/trigger timeline
Repeated CE count/rate and exact location within bounds
Clear command/result plus post-clear negative trigger and stable counters
Memory health, restored settings and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Persistent mode is enabled on only tuple 0:0:3 for a slot 1~N case, with no trigger, event bound, duration, clear command or post-clear verification. Two BIOS profiles conflict and threshold interaction is undefined; timeout is absent and Windows conflicts with dmesg.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Persistent implicit CE is identifiable. Engineering can provide target, bounds and authoritative clear semantics, so static review completes while execution is gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 50 Wistron-System RAS-00770-V003: provide slot-to-tuple coverage and approve/correct 0:0:3; define persistent mode arm/status, synthetic trigger, maximum count/rate/duration below thresholds, vendor clear/emergency-stop command and post-clear negative test; decide DRAM-versus-MCA profile; approve tool/spec provenance, CE Linux/Windows/BMC oracle, timeout, aborts, recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Reframes persistent injection as a bounded state lifecycle with verifiable clear and residual checks, preventing fault state from leaking into later cases.
independent_technical_reasoning: Persistent mode is not just a stronger one-shot; its safety depends on duration, access rate and interaction with corrected-error thresholds. A tool PASS at arm time says nothing about how many faults will be emitted or whether closing the process clears hardware state. The essential acceptance evidence is the transition from repeated expected events to no event after the documented clear, with counters stable during a verification access.
